status: exploratory — motivated by v1 in-sample results; must NOT be tested on v1 events
motivation: In v1 the CN equipment basket fell sharply on technology-wide rules (E09 Oct-2022: CAR[0,1] -23.9%) while entity-level additions showed no consistent sign. The v1 'domestic substitution' hypothesis (H2) pooled two mechanisms that may point in opposite directions.

rule_scope_definition.supply_chain: event cluster contains at least one BIS document tagged eventType=advanced_computing_semis by fr-tagger-v2 (technology- or country-wide controls on tools, chips, or US-person support)
rule_scope_definition.entity: event cluster contains only Entity List documents (named companies)

in_sample_descriptive_v1.note: Descriptive only, from research/event_study/export.py. Not evidence for v2.

test_sample.events: tightening BIS events whose event_instant is after 2026-09-22T00:00:00Z, collected by the PolicyOS federal_register backfill/cron and reviewed with the same rules as v1
test_sample.method: identical to hypotheses_v1.json (market model, [-250,-30] estimation, primary window [0,1], same baskets and event-day rule)
test_sample.earliest_evaluation: when either class has >= 8 out-of-sample events; report interim descriptive numbers yearly without inference

hypotheses.rationale: Tool/chip-wide controls constrain Chinese fabs' capex and US-person support, cutting domestic equipment demand expectations.
Named-customer restrictions redirect procurement to domestic vendors. Weak prior: v1 entity median was slightly negative.

known_limitations: Supply-chain rules are rare (3 in 2018–2026), so H4 may take years to reach n=8.
Scope classification depends on fr-tagger-v2; the tagger version is frozen for v2 evaluation.
Confounds (e.g. index-level rallies, earnings) are not controlled beyond the market model.
